transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with a deeply depressed mood for over a year, but over the last four weeks, things have suddenly shifted. I've been experiencing these confusing bursts of high energy, racing thoughts, and really unpredictable mood swings. It's just gotten very hard to manage on my own.
During these recent weeks of high energy, did it cause major problems in your work or relationships, or did you experience things like hearing voices or having unusual beliefs?

No, I've never heard voices or had any unusual beliefs. While I had overflowing energy and was extremely active during those four weeks, it didn't cause any major disruptions or severe problems in my work or relationships. I was just constantly on the go and doing a lot of things at once.
During those four weeks of high energy, did your family, friends, or coworkers notice a clear change in your behavior or comment on how different you were acting?

I'm not really sure if anyone noticed or commented on it, to be honest. I was so caught up in my own spinning thoughts and trying to keep up with all my activities that I didn't really pay attention to how others were reacting to me.
During those four weeks of high energy, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual—like feeling fully rested after only a few hours—without feeling tired?
I don't really recall having a reduced need for sleep during those four weeks. I didn't feel particularly rested on less sleep or notice any change like that.
During those four weeks of high energy, did you feel much more talkative than usual—like you couldn't stop talking—or did you feel an unusual boost in your self-confidence?

I don't recall being particularly talkative or feeling an unusual boost in my self-confidence during that time. I was mostly just focused on trying to keep up with my own racing thoughts and staying busy.
During those four weeks of high energy, did you find yourself easily distracted by unimportant things around you, or did you engage in risky behaviors like spending too much money?
No, I don't recall being easily distracted by things around me during those four weeks. I also didn't engage in any risky behaviors like overspending or anything like that.
You mentioned struggling with a depressed mood for over a year. Has this low mood been present most of the day, for more days than not, for a full two years or more?
No, it hasn't been going on for a full two years yet. This low mood has been present for about 1 year and 2 months now.
During this year and two months of low mood, have you also lost interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy, or struggled with low energy and feelings of worthlessness?

Yes, I have completely lost interest and pleasure in all the hobbies I used to enjoy, and I feel an extreme lack of both physical and mental energy. I wouldn't say I feel worthless specifically, but I do feel a deep sense of emptiness, emotional numbness, and complete indifference to any of my achievements.

Stafford/DSM-5 requires "abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood AND abnormally and persistently increased activity or energy").

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a history of a major depressive episode lasting 14 months (characterized by depressed mood, anhedonia, and lack of energy) followed by a 4-week period of abnormally elevated and irritable mood, increased activity/energy, and racing thoughts. This high-energy phase did not cause severe social or occupational impairment and lacked psychotic features, pointing to a hypomanic episode and confirming a diagnosis of Bipolar II Disorder.
